model_matrix.default: `agent --list-models --model gpt-5` -> "Loading models…" then "No models available for this account." exit 0. No arg-parse error; --model value accepted syntactically.
model_matrix.grok: `agent --list-models --model grok-4.5` -> identical output to default case: "No models available for this account." exit 0. No distinct error for this model id vs. the default; cannot confirm/deny grok-4.5 is a valid CLI model id at this layer.
model_matrix.invalid: `agent --list-models --model definitely-not-a-real-model` -> identical output: "No models available for this account." exit 0. No client-side validation of the --model value was observed; the CLI does not reject unknown model ids at the arg-parse layer, and the account-level "no models available" response masks whether server-side model-id validation would differ.

blocker:
Exact commands attempted and their verbatim (redacted) output: (1) `agent status` -> "Starting login process...
Checking authentication status...
✓ Login successful!
Logged in (unable to fetch user details)
(exit code 0)"; (2) `agent about` -> "User Email: Not logged in" (exit code 0); (3) `agent models` / `agent --list-models` (default, and with `--model grok-4.5`, and with `--model definitely-not-a-real-model`) -> "Loading models…
No models available for this account.
(exit code 0)" in all three cases. Net effect: the CLI self-reports a successful login but cannot resolve a user identity or any usable model for the account, so `agent --print` was intentionally not run to avoid spending against an account with no confirmed model access. Concrete preconditions to unblock: (a) a reachable CURSOR_API_KEY (or equivalent bearer credential) must be present in the session env so headless auth does not depend on the interactive `agent login` browser flow, which a sandboxed headless worker cannot complete; (b) the Cursor account tied to that credential must have at least one model provisioned/entitled, since `agent models` currently returns zero models regardless of --model value and there is no local keychain/session-store access available to this sandboxed worker to inspect or repair the account's session state directly.
